gpu-basics-memory-and-what-limits-infere.r: A 13B model loaded on a 24 GB card and crashed under real traffic. The cache for many long prompts used the remaining memory. Lower context limits, fewer concurrent requests and a larger card fixed it.
gpu-basics-memory-and-what-limits-infere.x: Capacity plan = weights + KV cache per token × context × concurrency + overhead. Prefill is compute bound, decode is bandwidth bound. Choose precision by measured quality, not by what fits.

serving-stacks-vllm-tgi-triton.r: A two-GPU server performed like one. vLLM had been started without tensor parallelism, so it used only the first card. Adding the flag split the model, enlarged the cache and about doubled throughput.
serving-stacks-vllm-tgi-triton.x: Choose the engine by model, hardware and skills, then tune from measurements on realistic traffic. Watch per-GPU utilization and cache size, pin versions, and keep weights on persistent storage with proper readiness probes.

gpus-on-kubernetes.r: A four-GPU job stayed Pending though eight GPUs were free. They were spread over four nodes with two each, and a pod must fit on one node. A pool of 8-GPU nodes for large jobs solved it.
gpus-on-kubernetes.x: GPU scheduling is bin packing on expensive nodes. Taint pools, scale them from zero, choose node shapes for the largest job, prefer MIG over time-slicing for production, and pin driver and operator versions together.

scaling-latency-and-cost.r: A launch spike caused timeouts while the autoscaler saw 12 percent CPU, because the work was on the GPU and 211 requests waited. Scaling on waiting requests, warm replicas and faster start-up fixed it.
scaling-latency-and-cost.x: Pick SLOs for TTFT and token rate, scale on queue depth and cache pressure, keep warm capacity for slow starts, and compare self-hosted cost per million tokens against hosted APIs at realistic utilisation.

monitoring-and-debugging-gpu-workloads.r: A four-GPU training job showed full utilization for six hours without progress. One worker had been evicted and the others waited for it inside NCCL. A job timeout and alert on running workers now fail it fast.
monitoring-and-debugging-gpu-workloads.x: Debug in order: visibility, memory and holders, thermals and clocks, XID and ECC in the kernel log, rank health and network, version compatibility. Alert on progress signals such as step rate, not only on utilization.

quantization-and-model-sizing.r: A team tried to run a 70-billion-parameter model on one 80 GB GPU in half precision and ran out of memory. Quantizing to 4 bits fit it with room for the cache, and a quality check showed acceptable results.
quantization-and-model-sizing.x: Sizing is arithmetic plus measurement. Do the memory math first, then test quality and throughput, because the cheapest format that meets your bar wins.

batching-kv-cache-and-throughput.r: A service was fast for one user and slow for fifty. Enabling continuous batching and sizing the cache for real concurrency tripled requests per second at the same p95 latency.
batching-kv-cache-and-throughput.x: Throughput and latency pull against each other. Decide your service level first, then tune batch limits to the highest load that still meets it.

multi-gpu-tensor-and-pipeline-parallelis.r: A team spread a model across GPUs on separate machines linked by ordinary networking, and throughput fell below a single GPU. Keeping tensor parallelism inside one node with fast links fixed it.
multi-gpu-tensor-and-pipeline-parallelis.x: Parallelism is a cost you pay only when memory forces you. Prefer the smallest split that fits, keep it inside a node and check the topology.

autoscaling-llm-inference.r: Traffic doubled at 9 a.m. and users saw timeouts for ten minutes while new GPU nodes joined and loaded the model. Keeping a small warm pool and scaling on queue depth removed the gap.
autoscaling-llm-inference.x: Slow startup makes scaling a forecasting problem. Pair reactive scaling with schedule-based or predictive warm capacity for known peaks.

model-loading-caching-and-cold-starts.r: A rolling update restarted all replicas at once and each downloaded 140 GB from the internet. A local cache and a slower rollout kept capacity during the change.
model-loading-caching-and-cold-starts.x: Start-up time is an availability issue. Anything that makes a replica slow to return should be treated like a dependency of the rollout.

gpu-sharing-mig-and-time-slicing.r: Fifty small notebooks each held a full GPU and left most idle. MIG slices let seven jobs share each card with fixed memory, and the same hardware served more users.
gpu-sharing-mig-and-time-slicing.x: Utilization is a cost lever, but sharing without isolation moves risk onto neighbours. Match the sharing method to how much each workload can tolerate interference.

gpu-failures-xid-errors-and-recovery.r: Training jobs failed with a mysterious error every few hours. DCGM showed uncorrectable ECC errors on one GPU. Draining that node and replacing the card ended the failures.
gpu-failures-xid-errors-and-recovery.x: At scale some GPU will always be failing. Detect fast, remove the node automatically and keep spare capacity so a failure is a ticket, not an incident.
